title: How LEGO Really Makes Money (From Near-Bankruptcy to Toy Giant)
description:
LEGO brought in DKK 83.5 billion (about $12 billion) in 2025 — and around 26% of it became operating profit. Twenty years ago it was losing money fast. In this file we open the money machine behind LEGO: a carpenter's workshop in Billund, the 1958 stud-and-tube patent, the 2003 crash, the Knudstorp rescue, Star Wars and other borrowed heroes, the 18+ adult sets, family ownership and the latest numbers.

{CHAPTERS}

Sources: LEGO Group 2025 annual results release (March 2026); LEGO Group first-half 2026 results (via Toys n Playthings); LEGO.com history pages (the LEGO name, the stud-and-tube principle, quality, the beginning of the LEGO Group); LEGO.com ownership page; LEGO Company 2003 and 2004 annual result releases; Reuters via NZ Herald (LEGOLAND sale, 2005); Entrepreneur/Business Insider; Fortune (adult fans, Circana data).

All figures are from company reports where available and are rounded; the ~26% margin is our own arithmetic (operating profit divided by revenue). The dollar figure is an approximate conversion. This video is for education only, not investment advice.
